source.title: SLDBench v2: Active Scaling Law Discovery
source.authors: Ling-Bei Meng; Rui Huang; Zhi-Rong Shen; Jin-Xin Liu; Lin Jing; Hao-Rui Chen; Yao-Song Du; Haowei Lin

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates prediction on hidden, larger-scale experiments from completed records, including fits of a fixed power-law reference to selected subsets. It uses a benchmark and agent-discovery procedure rather than reproducing the original scaling-law experiments.
record.gate_note: The study tests held-out extrapolation, but the agent law form is open-ended and the benchmark spans heterogeneous targets, not only held-out language-model pretraining loss. Its 30 tasks were deliberately selected because the reference power-law fit scored R2 ≤ 0.8 in both settings. The non-agent baselines fit the reference law to purchased subsets and score it on hidden targets. Cited results about other scaling-law studies are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: This is an agent benchmark. Held-out extrapolation is the task given to agents, and the scores measure agent law-discovery and acquisition, not whether scaling laws hold. Agent laws are open-ended, not necessarily power laws. The only power-law fits (reference law) run on 30 tasks kept because that law already scored R2 ≤ 0.8. Its low held-out R2 is therefore a selection artefact, not evidence on V2. Targets also mix LM loss, downstream accuracy, vision–language error, protein LMs and others, with no per-task power-law result for LM pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that agents nearly identical in Passive SLD separate widely in Active SLD. The loss comes from what is bought, not sequential access. Cheap purchases leave conditions needed for extrapolation unobserved, and cost alone does not determine quality. Under a fixed law, within-group scale variation matters more than reaching every group. Agents that pick experiments to discriminate between candidate laws are proposed as a next step.
record.recipe_differences: This is an agent benchmark for jointly acquiring records and constructing an open-ended predictive law, using historical experiment replay and hidden-target R2. The reference baseline is a bounded multi-start additive power-law fit, not a reproduction of the original studies' training experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction quality varies with passive versus active access, acquisition rule and budget, agent system, task, and repeat. The study reports that within-system outcomes can vary substantially across repeats.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a fixed reference power law on screened tasks, which subset is fitted matters a lot. Price-spread selection raises median R2 to −0.005 vs −1.456 for cheapest-per-group at 2% budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling-law extrapolation quality depends on sampling scale variation within each group, more than on covering all groups (data-selection dependence of fits).

fits_no_version.finding: Frontier agents score similarly with all data (median R2 0.72–0.75) but spread widely when buying data (0.24–0.57). Cost is not one-to-one with quality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM agents' scaling-law discovery degrades under active, cost-aware experiment selection.

record.problems: The difficulty screen intentionally retains only tasks on which one reference law scores R2 ≤ 0.8, so results are not representative of the full corpus. The 30 tasks mix targets and domains, prices include estimates and proxies, and agent evaluation covers 8 systems with three repeats. The study reports source-bootstrap intervals for error multipliers, but Table 1 medians and Table 7 rule medians do not include uncertainty intervals.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted system-by-system threshold shares in Table 5, detailed purchase-coverage statistics in Tables 8–10, task-specific case-study rows in Tables 11–12, and best@3 results in Table 6. They are secondary or duplicate summaries of the held-out prediction and acquisition findings captured above; no individual task-level results were added.

untested.parts: No test of power-law loss vs N, D or C.
No unselected test of whether small-run power-law fits predict larger runs; the only power-law fits are on tasks screened for fit failure.
No shape comparison at fixed parameters.
Non-text tasks exist but no per-domain test of power-law form.
Downstream targets appear, but no result on their predictability with scale.
Exponent or allocation changes under fitting choices not measured.

record.verdict_notes: Cites Kaplan and Hoffmann as motivation only. The reader's V2 'challenges' label rests on reference-law fits on tasks selected because that law fails (R2 ≤ 0.8). The authors say the screen favors tasks where it fails and is not representative, so the label is removed. Agent and model names are as given in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute across several orders of magnitude with the other quantities non-bottlenecked.

The agent laws are not restricted to power laws, and results are aggregated across heterogeneous tasks rather than reported specifically for language-model pretraining loss. The study does not establish a general prediction result across all larger-run scales.
Does not estimate compute-optimal parameter and token counts or their growth exponents.
Does not compare architecture depth, width, or other architectural choices at fixed parameter count.
Although the benchmark includes non-text and other training settings, it does not test whether the same power-law form holds across modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Some benchmark targets are downstream metrics, but the study does not report whether downstream performance itself improves predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
Does not measure changes in fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations under alternative parameter-counting, fitting, or training-schedule choices, nor directly test curve bending.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Reference power-law fit on selected subsets at 0.5%–2% of pool cost
reader_labels.reason: Across acquisition rules, median held-out R2 is below zero at these budgets, showing poor extrapolation on the benchmark's deliberately challenging tasks (rows ref_cheapest_05 through ref_spread_2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Agent extrapolation and reference-law fits across the selected benchmark tasks
reader_labels.reason: Agent predictions are better with all outcomes than under active acquisition, and reference-law results remain modest even at larger partial-data budgets; the study's selected-task design limits generalization (agent and reference-law rows).
